full_judgment:
6. Defendant Nos.1-4 contested the said suit by filing a written statement denying the material averments made in the plaint and contending inter alia, that the suit property belonged to Raja Mahendra Ranjan Roy Chowdhury. He appointed Puma Chandra Adhikary as the 'Purohit' in his house. As the consideration for his religious service Raja Mahendra Ranjan gave him nishkar pattan of 1.19 acres of land of CS Khatian No.176 for permanently residing therein as well as for maintenance of his livelihood. Accordingly, the said land described in Schedule 'Kha' was recorded in his name in CS Khatian No.176. He possessed 22 decimals of the land of Plot No.69 by making a homestead thereon, by performing religious rites towards the Deity established in the land of Plot No.70 and by cultivating 91 decimals of the land of Plot No.67. RS Khatian No.188 was duly published in his name. At the request of the people in general belonging to the Hindu Religion, Puma Chandra dedicated, by registered Deed of Gift No.6704 dated 6-11-1996, 32 decimals of land from Plot No.67 and 52 decimals from Plot No.91 to the Radha-Gobinda Deity. He died leaving behind his three sons namely, Prabhat, Ashutosh and Shachin. Shachin and Ashutosh gifted their share to defendant No.4 by registered Deed of Gift No.1657 dated 25-2-1998. The defendants have title and possession over the 'Ka' schedule land. The defendants have been possessing the shops established in the suit land and also filed Other Suit No.110 of 2002 for a decree of permanent injunction as the plaintiff threatened to forcibly dispossess them from the suit property. The plaintiff has no title and possession in the suit land and hence, the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

 20. Now during the hearing, the learned Advocate for the opposite parties candidly submits that factually the opposite parties possess only 07 decimals of land.But, it appears from the deposition of DW 1 that they are no more Purohit of the Deity rather, they are engaged in the photo framing business. Thus, they cannot claim any portion of the debutter property in the capacity of purohit. The Sebait also cannot transfer any debutter property. On these points, in the case of Bangladesh vs Abdul Hye and others, 24 BLT (AD) 340 the Appellate Division held that a 'Poojari' is a servant of the Sebait, and no part of the rights and obligations of the latter are transferrable to him. When the appointment of a 'Purohit' has been at the will of the founder, the mere fact that the appointee has performed the worship for several generations will not confer an independent right upon the members of the family so appointed and will not entitle them as of right to be continued in office as priests. Thus, the suit property was not transferrable by the Sebait in favour of Puma Chandra predecessor of the defendants nor can they claim any title in the suit property as of right as the sons of the then 'Purohit'. Both the Courts below failed to consider that the Debutter property cannot be claimed as personal property by any person whatever might be his status. Accordingly, both the Courts below also failed to appreciate that the subsequent SA and BRS records prepared in the names of the opposite parties, or their predecessor have no legal basis inasmuch as the entire property being debutter property without any reservation, the same is beyond the scope and application of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 as per section 20(5)(ii)(c) thereof and accordingly, nobody can claim any tenancy right in the debutter property under the Government.
